input.summary: Original data are unavailable, so reanalysis is not feasible. Instead, a bounded emulated-netem pilot is proposed: two TCP flows are run with and without 20 ms added delay under a fixed bottleneck, measuring flow completion time to test whether delay changes FCT. Protocol is null pending three owner decisions on bottleneck rate, file size, and CCA.
clarification_questions: What bottleneck link rate (Mbit/s) and buffer size (kbytes) should be used for the emulated conditions?
What file size(s) (Mbytes) should each client transfer, and how many replications per configuration are desired?
Which TCP congestion control algorithm(s) should be tested (e.g., cubic, bbr, reno)?

proposal.problem: The original recorded data from the paper are unavailable, making direct reanalysis impossible. An independent emulated measurement is the only feasible path to assess the claim.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms one-way delay change TCP flow completion time relative to a zero-delay baseline?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions: (1) baseline — 0 ms added delay; (2) treatment — 20 ms added delay. All other bottleneck parameters (rate, buffer, loss, CCA, file size) held constant across conditions.
proposal.related_work: No reviewed citations are available from the supplied source metadata. The claim is described as synthetic; no prior empirical values are asserted here.
proposal.alternatives: The observed FCT difference (if any) could reflect RTT-driven slow-start elongation, retransmission timeout inflation, or bufferbloat interactions rather than a simple additive delay effect. These mechanisms are untested alternatives.
proposal.design: Independent-check emulated pilot using netem_nines.py with two clients. One configuration sets client_delays_ms to [0, 0] (baseline) and another to [20, 20] (treatment). FCT is recorded per flow per replication. Owner must confirm bottleneck rate, buffer, file size, CCA, and replication count before the protocol can be frozen.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (ms) per client per replication. Comparison: distribution of FCT under 0 ms delay vs. 20 ms delay.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck rate, buffer size, loss percentage (0%), CCA, file size, and number of clients are held fixed across conditions. Only delay varies.
proposal.falsification: The claim is falsified if FCT distributions under 0 ms and 20 ms delay are indistinguishable (e.g., overlapping ranges with no consistent directional shift across replications). It is supported if a consistent directional difference is observed in every replication.
proposal.inputs: Emulated network environment via netem_nines.py runner. No original paper data or author implementation is required. Bottleneck rate, buffer, file size, CCA, and replication count must be supplied by the owner.
proposal.limitations: Emulated results are simulation evidence, not real-world measurements. The claim source is synthetic and unreviewed; generalization to any real network or paper finding is not warranted. A pilot cannot establish causality or broader generalization. Original data remain unavailable; reanalysis is not possible.
